mechanism: The cued base's errors that RL avoids are committed in the first ~1,500 answer tokens (reading the givens and choosing the plan), where a lower temperature makes the base choose better, while its T 0.6 loops only start late in long self-similar text; so one global temperature has to trade early plan accuracy (better at T 0.6) against late loop freedom (better at T 1.0), and RL, being temperature-flat, does not face that trade.
starts_from: knowledge-13cff3 (on the 402 problems the cued base finishes at T 0.6, T 1.0 gets only 361-364 against 378 right), result-afc423 (first wrong step at a median 0.20 of the answer), result-c495fe (a misreading has already cost 32 points before its sentence), result-a6ab7a (RL's edge is in the text by the 25-50 % cut). Observation explained: T 0.6 finished answers are more often right than T 1.0 answers to the same problems, yet T 0.6 loses overall.
differs_from: r2-external-2 and r2-across-1 set temperature by per-token entropy (forks vs near-deterministic tokens), and the egate arms tested exactly that; here the switch is set by position in the answer, not by entropy. r3-revise-2 (loops open at impasses) says samplers act only through loops; m01 says T 0.6 also improves early choices on problems with no loop. m05 says T 0.6 and T 1.0 fail on different problems; m01 says the same problem benefits from T 0.6 early and T 1.0 late, so a fixed schedule beats choosing a temperature per problem.
holds_against: result-34897a (entropy-gated T 0.6 at confident positions or at forks gives 33-44 cap hits and no gain): those arms sharpened every part of the answer, so loops still formed late; m01 keeps T 1.0 after the early segment, where loops begin. facts r7-m03 (the self-inconsistent-equation rate at T 1.0 is 0.36 times the T 0.6 rate): that counts arithmetic equations over whole finished answers, while m01's errors are early reading and plan choices (median position 0.20), which that count does not measure.
base_change: Sampling by position: T 0.6 / top-p 1.0 for the first 1,500 generated tokens of each answer, then T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 to the 16,384 cap; same prompt and cue, one sample (predicted 418-424 of 500 on MATH-500 at about 4,100 tokens per problem, against 410.5).
first_test: Fetch the full-text T 0.6 / top-p 1.0 cued-base rows (iterate-runs abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa/answers.jsonl). On each of its cap hits compute rule-A onset (first line-start p with zlib ratio of text[p:p+8000] < 0.10) and convert it to a token position as n_new * p / len(text). Statistic 1: share of rule-A onsets before token 1,500; m01 predicts at most 0.10 and is refuted above 0.25. Statistic 2: join with day1_3 math500_base_cue-01 rows (attempt 0, samples 0-3) and t1_t2_items per_problem.json; on problems finished in d4fa, compute d4fa accuracy minus mean T 1.0 accuracy separately in the top half of t2_generated_tokens; m01 predicts the T 0.6 edge is at least +3 points there as well (refuted if it is <= 0 in the long half while positive in the short half).

mechanism: The cued base loses long and medium problems by switching lines of attack too early (writing 'Alternatively', 'Let me try a different approach' before the current line is finished), which leaves abandoned partial derivations and an answer taken from the last, least-developed attempt, whereas RL-Zero-Math learned to stay on one line and verify it; so the base's wrong finished answers carry more switch markers than its right siblings of the same length, and penalising switch tokens recovers part of the gap.
starts_from: result-afc423 (wrong plan 28 % of base finished-wrong; base wrong samples longer than right siblings, r5-m02 test +0.193 log ratio), result-855858 (RL writes more wait/hmm/actually, which do not separate right from wrong), result-f21d2e (length alone predicts a wrong base answer with AUROC 0.831). Observation explained: within a problem the base's longer finished samples are the wrong ones, while extra checking words carry no signal.
differs_from: result-855858 and r4-m06 / r6-m05 are about hold-on words (Wait, Hmm), that is checks within one line; m02 is about abandoning a line (thought switches), a different marker class that has never been counted. r2-revise-2 (weak error detector) and r5-m05 (restating after Wait) concern what happens after a check; m02 concerns leaving a line before it is checked. m10 says length hurts RL beyond an optimum; m02 says switching hurts the base at any length.
holds_against: result-855858 (checking markers do not separate right and wrong samples of the same problem): it counted wait/hmm/actually, which 2501.18585 separates from thought-switch markers; switch markers are the class that tracks failure there. r4-m11 refuted (0 of the base's v3-wrong answers have a right first answer marker): a switch abandons a line before it reaches a stated answer, so m02 predicts no right earlier answer marker, only abandoned partial work.
base_change: Decoding: a logit penalty of 3 nats on the first token of switch phrases (' Alternatively', ' Another', ' Instead', and 'try a different' continuations) for 600 tokens after each switch, the TIP rule of 2501.18585, on the cued base at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, one sample (predicted +3 to +5 points on MATH-500 at about the same tokens).
first_test: Fetch the full-text day1_3 rows of the cued base (iterate-runs abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b) and of RL (abaybektursun-1114-183640-e828), attempt 0. Count per 1,000 generated tokens the matches of r'\b(Alternatively|Another approach|Another way|Let me try (a )?(different|another)|Let's try (a )?(different|another)|Instead, let)' . Statistic 1: base rate / RL rate on finished answers; m02 predicts >= 1.5 (refuted below 1.15). Statistic 2: on problems where the base has both a finished right and a finished wrong sample, the within-problem ratio of switch counts, wrong over right, after dividing by tokens; m02 predicts >= 1.4 (refuted below 1.1).

mechanism: RL-Zero-Math opens by restating the problem's givens almost verbatim before working, which gives later steps an exact in-context copy to read numbers and conditions from by induction-style copying; the cued base mostly jumps straight into a paraphrased plan, so it later reads givens from its own paraphrase, and that is where its misreadings (the error class RL lowers most, -1.52 nats) come from.
starts_from: result-faf15a (Math-RL lowers the base's misread steps by 1.52 nats, slips 0.72, wrong plans not at all), result-c495fe (a misreading has already cost 32 points before its quoted sentence), result-a497ff (from before the wrong step, misreadings 27 -> 36 of 84 with problem contrast), result-a6ab7a (RL's advantage sits in the first quarter to half of the text). Observation explained: misreadings are fixed by RL and are set up before the sentence that shows them.
differs_from: r7-m05 (no gain) says misread and slip steps are what the prior writes for a generic problem; m03 makes no claim about where the wrong token comes from but names a behaviour (an early verbatim restatement) whose absence lets it through, and predicts a text statistic r7-m05 never measured. m06 puts the loss of fidelity late in long answers; m03 puts it at the opening, so the two predict opposite positions of misreads. r5-m10 and its rival concern the 3-token opening register, not what the first few hundred tokens copy.
holds_against: r7-m05 (no gain; deleting the problem raises misread and wrong-plan steps alike, 0.686 and 0.688): that equal rise fits a generic context effect and does not contradict a protective restatement; m03 is tested by restatement coverage, which differs between models. result-a497ff (problem-contrast decoding before the wrong step adds only +1.6 points): contrast acts at the wrong step, after the paraphrase has replaced the givens in the recent context; m03 predicts the fix must come at the opening.
base_change: Prompt: extend the prefilled cue to ' line!\n\nOkay, so the problem says:' so that the base starts by restating the givens, at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, one sample (predicted +2 to +4 points on MATH-500, all of it on problems whose base errors are misreadings, at +100 to +200 tokens per problem).
first_test: Fetch the full-text day1_3 rows with prompts (iterate-runs abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b base cue; abaybektursun-1114-183640-e828 RL). For each answer, coverage = share of the distinct numbers and single-letter variables in the problem text (from the prompt field) that appear in the first 1,200 characters of the answer. Statistic 1: mean coverage RL minus base over attempt-0 finished answers; m03 predicts >= 0.15 (refuted below 0.05). Statistic 2: join studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/judge-01/labels.json (model base, passA label containing 'misread'); coverage of those samples minus the mean coverage of right siblings of the same problem; m03 predicts <= -0.10 (refuted if >= 0).

mechanism: Solved examples in the context change the cued base mainly by setting its prior over answer length and closing habits: examples that are long and end with an explicit re-check make the base write longer, checked answers on problems it can already solve, which removes quick finished-wrong answers (the base's 3/4 -> RL 4/4 cell); the RL-written draw 1 helped and draw 2 did not because the two sets differ in length and checking, not in who wrote them or in subject.
starts_from: result-6d422d and result-5227b9 (RL-written draw 1 +5.7, draw 2 -0.6, draw 1 minus draw 2 +6.3 [2.6, 9.9]; draw-1 examples 8,240 tokens vs base-written 4,853; cap hits 31 vs 17), result-afc423 (43 % of the gap is base 3/4 -> RL 4/4). Observation explained: why one set of three RL texts gave 28 more right answers than another set by the same writer (left open on the board; no graveyard theory explained it).
differs_from: r7-m12 (refuted) said examples transfer a subject routine; m04 says they transfer a length and closing prior, spread over subjects. r5-m10-rival and m03 concern the opening; m04 concerns the expected total length and the closing check. m07 says RL's weight directions move length toward a target; m04 is a prompt-side length prior with no weight change, and predicts that the base's own long answers work as well as RL's.
holds_against: result-5227b9 (RL-written draw 2 gives -0.6 and the hard328 draw-1 arm 164 = base): on MATH-500 m04 attributes draw 2's null to shorter or less-checked examples, and on hard328 a longer length prior adds cap hits (107 vs 77) that cancel the gain on solvable problems, as observed. facts r7-m12 (same-subject minus other-subject gain -0.018): m04 predicts no subject effect, consistent.
base_change: Prompt: three of the cued base's own MATH-train answers chosen without labels as the longest answers that agree with their own 4-sample vote and contain a closing re-check, placed in context before the cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, one sample (predicted +3 to +5 points on MATH-500, concentrated on problems the base solves 3 of 4, at about the same generated tokens).
first_test: Fetch the shots rows (iterate-runs abaybektursun-1114-183901-fd89, RL-written draw 1, and the RL-written draw-2 job among abaybektursun-1114-195357-6936 / -195350-bc00, identified by shots_arm). Drop problems 0-2. Statistic 1: on problems finished in both arms, median n_new of draw 1 divided by median n_new of draw 2; m04 predicts >= 1.2 (refuted below 1.05). Statistic 2: split by k = right count in the 4 day1_3 base cue samples; the draw-1 minus draw-2 gain in the k = 3 stratum divided by the total draw-1 minus draw-2 gain; m04 predicts >= 0.4, and the number of quick finished-wrong answers (<= 2,000 tokens) in draw 1 at most 0.6 times draw 2's.

mechanism: The cued base's two temperatures fail on largely different problems: at T 0.6 it loses long problems to self-reinforcing loops, at T 1.0 it loses short and medium problems to finished wrong answers; RL fails on neither set; so the base's failures at a single temperature are correlated across samples (a 4-sample vote at T 1.0 stalls below its independent-slip prediction), while one T 0.6 attempt with a loop stop and a T 1.0 resample on a detected loop recovers part of the gap at RL's tokens.
starts_from: knowledge-13cff3 (T 0.6 finishes 402 problems with 378 right; resampling its 98 cap hits at T 1.0 gives 426 mean at 5,138 tokens with loop stop), result-e41d94 (vote 10 problems below the independent-slip prediction; 8 more 0-of-4 problems than binomial), knowledge-9e4147 (plain base loses 28 points at T 1.0 on short problems and none on the longest). Observation explained: votes over same-temperature samples stall even though the base has right samples elsewhere.
differs_from: result-5da8a9 (one axis) compared arms all sampled at T 1.0; m05 claims a second axis that appears only between temperatures. m01 schedules temperature by position inside one answer; m05 chooses it per problem from whether a loop fires, and predicts no gain from low temperature on problems that do not loop at T 0.6. r3-revise-2 (no claims) said samplers move accuracy only through loops; m05 also says T 1.0 costs finished accuracy on short problems, a non-loop failure.
holds_against: result-5da8a9 (36 arms show no excess union over the difficulty-matched null): every arm there was a T 1.0 sample, where failure types coincide; the T 0.6 cell was not included. result-34897a (all entropy-gated mixtures stay 1.3-1.4 points under T 1.0): those mix temperatures within an answer and so get loops and slips together; m05's gain needs the loop stop and a fresh T 1.0 draw.
base_change: Sampling and selection: draw one T 0.6 / top-p 1.0 answer, stop it when loop rule A fires, and only then draw one T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 answer; keep the finished one (predicted 424-430 of 500 on MATH-500 at about 5,100 tokens per problem against RL's 4,675).
first_test: Use the T 0.6 rows (iterate-runs abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa, score_v3, cap_hit) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (attempt 0, samples 0-3). Right = score_v3 == 1 and no cap hit. Statistic: mean over s in {0..3} of |right in d4fa OR right in T 1.0 sample s| minus mean over the 6 pairs (s, s') of |right in s OR right in s'|; m05 predicts >= +8 problems (refuted below +3). Secondary: among problems wrong at T 0.6 and right in at least 2 T 1.0 samples, the share that are T 0.6 cap hits; m05 predicts >= 0.7.

mechanism: The cued base's hold on the problem's givens weakens with distance in tokens from the problem text (no input norms and long math contexts make its attention to the prompt fade), so numbers and conditions drift as an answer grows and misreadings are more frequent late in long answers; RL attends back to the prompt at every length, so the base's gap grows with answer length even on problems it understands at the start.
starts_from: knowledge-9e4147 (gap in every RL-length quartile, largest in the longest: -20.0 points), result-5de032 (hard328 by RL-length quartile 78/82, 52/67, 30/45, 4/12), result-faf15a (misreadings lowered most by RL), result-51fd20 (the base's long answers are failures to solve, not to stop). Observation explained: the gap rises with length even where neither model hits the cap.
differs_from: r6-m01 (refuted) had the register held by attention to the cue fade; m06 is about the givens, not the register, and predicts drift of values with the register intact. all-1 / r1-all-1 (refuted) had a general degradation of the next-token distribution with own-text length; m06 predicts that only reading of givens degrades, so slips and plans do not rise with position. m03 puts the misreading at the opening; m06 late.
holds_against: r6-m01 refuted (0.7 % of long answers show textbook headers): register decay is not needed; m06 predicts the base keeps deliberating while its numbers drift. result-c495fe (a misreading has already cost 32 points before its sentence): drift is gradual, so the answer is already off track before the sentence the judge quotes; m06 is consistent with an early loss as long as misreads located later in the answer are more common.
base_change: Decoding with a context edit: every 3,000 generated tokens, insert the problem text again into the base's context as a quoted block ('(Re-reading the problem: ...)') and continue sampling at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0; the inserted tokens are prompt-side, so generated tokens stay about the same (predicted +2 to +3 points on MATH-500, all in answers longer than 3,000 tokens).
first_test: From studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/math500-01/items.json (51 base items with position and label) and studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/judge-01/labels.json (base rows with proxy_position and passA label), compute the share of first wrong steps labelled misread among those located after 40 % of the answer divided by the same share among those before 40 %. m06 predicts >= 1.8 (refuted below 1.2). Secondary: the same ratio for RL rows in labels.json; m06 predicts it is below the base's.

mechanism: Revision of across-2: the top singular directions of any GRPO-style RL-Zero delta (Math, Code, IF) write a reward-agnostic length prior that pulls every answer's length toward one target of a few thousand tokens, lengthening short answers and cutting long ones, a by-product of length-normalised policy-gradient losses rather than of 3.1's truncated-as-negative training; the accuracy gain of the finish dial is the base's own precision at the new lengths.
starts_from: result-1b6bf2 (top-8 raises p10 by 32-72 % and cuts the p90 tail), result-51a0e7 and result-6f1bb7 (cap hits follow the size of the 8 directions; right answers per finished answer stay near 0.65; IF and Math 3.0 directions also finish), result-e2482e (late readouts 'Okay, consider' vs 'perhaps, maybe'). Observation explained: one set of directions both lengthens short answers and shortens long ones.
differs_from: across-2 / r1-across-2 (refuted: claimed 8 word-salad tails at a = 1.5, measured 34) put a stop/deliberation controller trained by 3.1's truncation penalty in late layers and said over-dosing stays coherent; m07 drops both: the prior comes from length normalisation in any run (IF 3.0 too) and over-dosing pushes lengths past the target into degeneracy (size 3: 117 right). all-2 / r1-all-2 said a saturating answer-mode switch; m07 says a graded length target. m08 says an additive end hazard that only shortens; m07 also lengthens short answers.
holds_against: r1-across-2 (measured 34 word-salad tails at a = 1.5 against a claimed 8): m07 expects over-shoot to degrade text, which is what that count shows. result-6f1bb7 (IF's 8 directions cut cap hits but leave 158 unboxed short answers): a reward-agnostic length prior predicts IF also finishes; its answer format comes from the rest of the IF update, not from the length directions.
first_test: Join studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json (n_generated, cap_hit) with studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (t1 and t2 tokens, cap hits). On problems finished in both top8 and T1 (cued base), regress ln(top8 tokens) on ln(T1 tokens). m07 predicts slope <= 0.6 with a fixed point (where the fitted line crosses equality) between 2,500 and 8,000 tokens (refuted if slope >= 0.85 or the line lies above equality everywhere). Control: the same regression of rand8_plain-01 against the plain base T3 tokens (rln4/t1_t3_items-01) has slope >= 0.85.

mechanism: The finishing part of the RL-Math delta adds a roughly fixed amount to the per-token log-odds of closing an answer, at a cost in finished-answer precision that grows with the dose; a host whose own ending hazard is lower (Think-SFT, trained on long teacher traces) therefore needs about twice the dose the base needs before cap hits stop being its main loss, which is why Think-SFT + a(RL - base) peaks near a = 2 while the base's top-8 edit peaks near 1.5.
starts_from: result-3387ce (Think-SFT + a(RL - base): cap hits 94.5, 75, 54, 44, 33 for a = 0..4; right-of-finished 88 -> 72 %; peak at a = 2), result-6f1bb7 (base top-8 dial peaks at 1.5 with 25 cap hits), result-818c20 (Think-SFT 29 % cap hits on hard328, finished answers 88 % right). Observation explained: why the best dose differs between hosts (no graveyard theory addressed the transplant peak).
differs_from: r1-across-2 and across-2 put the controller in the base-vs-RL gap and predicted coherent over-dosing; m08 is about how the dose transfers between hosts. m07 says a length target that also lengthens short answers; m08 says only the closing hazard moves, so it predicts the dose ratio between hosts from their hazards and says nothing about short answers. r3-external-2 (ExPO-style over-shoot) had the optimal scale shrink with training; m08 has it grow as the host's own hazard falls.
holds_against: result-1b6bf2 (the top-8 edit lengthens short answers, p10 +32-72 %): m08 concerns the tail hazard only and leaves the short-answer change to another part of the delta; its test uses the tail alone. result-3387ce (right-of-finished falls from 88 to 72 % as a rises): m08 needs that cost; the optimum is where the hazard gain stops paying for it.
first_test: From studies/rlneurons/results/transplant/hard328-01/rows.jsonl (arms think = a 0, sft1_rl10 to sft1_rl40, sft1_rnd10) fit an exponential ending hazard per arm, h = finished answers / total generated tokens (cap hits censored at 16,384), and regress ln h on a. m08 predicts the fit is near linear (R^2 >= 0.9 over a = 0..4) and the noise arm at a = 0 level. Then compute the same slope on MATH-500 from the theta(a) cue rows of the day1_wdiff jobs (iterate-runs abaybektursun-1114-*, a = 0.25 to 1.5, n_new and cap_hit). m08 predicts the ratio of the two slopes within [0.6, 1.6] (refuted outside [0.4, 2.5]).

mechanism: Revision of r7-m09: Think-SFT, copying its teacher traces, often writes 'Answer:' and then puts the value on the next line, which grader v3's last-marker rule reads as an empty or wrong answer at every difficulty level, not only on easy problems or non-integer answers; adding the RL-Math delta switches the hybrid to RL's single \boxed{} ending, so Think-SFT + 2(RL - base) gains about 4 problems per 500 from grading alone.
starts_from: result-818c20 (16 of Think-SFT's 74 finished wrong MATH-500 answers end in a line equal to the gold, on the line after 'Answer:'; RL 0 of 131; v3 undercounts by about 4 per sample), knowledge-499152 (v3's 'Answer:' marker handling), result-3387ce (the hybrid). Observation explained: Think-SFT's finished-wrong answers contain the gold far more often than RL's.
differs_from: r7-m09 (no gain: recurrence 0.167 on n 6, non-integer share 0.33, cap share 0.33) said a teacher final format (units, words, several boxes, prose) is rejected on easy, non-integer problems; m09 names a different cause, a line break after 'Answer:', predicts it at all difficulty levels and answer types, and predicts it disappears with the RL delta. r4-m12 (refuted) concerned non-canonical forms in the base's answers; m09 concerns Think-SFT's layout. knowledge-4662c6 is a period bug of at most 0.1 point.
holds_against: r7-m09 no gain (its recurrence and non-integer tests on 6 easy problems): m09 makes no prediction about recurrence across prompts or answer type on easy problems; its claim is about the layout over all finished answers. result-0018d3 and result-dba8ee (no wrong answer accepted by v3 and 112 of 113 flips right): those read base and RL rows, whose layouts v3 handles; Think-SFT rows were not in those reads.
first_test: Fetch the full-text Think-SFT hard328 single-sample jobs (iterate-runs abaybektursun-1115-000503-1e5f, -000525-ea4e, -014823-ef56, -014833-1daa). Among finished v3-wrong answers, compute the share whose first non-empty line after the last 'Answer:' (or the last line if no marker) agrees with gold under rln4_lib.agree. m09 predicts >= 0.08 on hard328 (refuted below 0.03), and the same share for RL plain hard328 full text (abaybektursun-1114-200505-5ff2) <= 0.01. Also report the share by cued-base solve count k (from day1_3 hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01): m09 predicts no fall from k >= 3 to k <= 1.

mechanism: Each model has an inverted-U of within-problem accuracy against answer length whose peak sits where its training traces were long: RL-Zero-Math's peak is at a few thousand tokens and its answers past about 8,000 tokens are mostly unsupported finishes, while Think-SFT, imitating long teacher traces, keeps its precision to 16,000 tokens and beyond; so the Think-SFT-over-RL lead grows with the length a problem demands and with the token cap.
starts_from: result-527fbb (an RL answer over 8,000 tokens is right 12.5 points less often than its shorter answers to the same problem, Think-SFT's +1.2), result-b006f5 (finished answers over 12,000 tokens right 68.2 % Think-SFT, 24.4 % RL), result-389164 (stopped at 14,028 tokens Think-SFT is level with RL). Observation explained: the reward-free model beats RL only on long answers to hard problems.
differs_from: r6-account-rival (no RL-specific finishing policy; one difficulty axis) says a stronger arm wins at its strength everywhere; m10 says the ordering of RL and Think-SFT flips with demanded length. r5-m04 (refuted) said Think-SFT fails by cap hits on RL's longest problems; m10 says it wins there given the tokens. m12 is a constant per-token solve hazard for one model; m10 is a peaked accuracy-length curve that differs between models.
holds_against: result-02da9f (among long finished wrong answers RL and the base assert equally often, 72.5 vs 66.2 %): m10 does not need a higher assertion rate among wrong answers, only lower precision past RL's peak, which result-fc7efc shows (RL finishes long and wrong far more often, 381 vs 281). result-389164 (Think-SFT stopped at 14,028 tokens is level with RL stopped there, +0.1): that is what m10 predicts, since the lead sits beyond that length.
first_test: From studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl (attempt 0, finished samples), demean right/wrong within problem and model, bin by n_new (0-2k, 2-4k, 4-8k, 8-12k, 12-16.4k), and find each model's bin of highest demeaned accuracy. m10 predicts RL's peak at or below 4-8k and Think-SFT's at 8-12k or above, with RL's 12-16k bin at least 15 points below its peak and Think-SFT's within 5 points of its peak (refuted if Think-SFT's peak bin is at or below RL's).

mechanism: Think-SFT inherited from its multilingual teacher traces a drift into Chinese in long reasoning, and once it switches it rarely reaches a right finished answer, so most of its cap hits are drifted traces that more tokens will not rescue; adding the RL-Math delta, learned from English-only rollouts that collapsed onto one output style, suppresses the drift and turns those traces into finished answers.
starts_from: result-818c20 (Think-SFT cap hits are unfinished reasoning, not loops: rule A 6 of 378, 86 switch into Chinese; finished answers right 88 %), result-3387ce (the RL delta makes Think-SFT finish), result-bce075 (RL finishing Think-SFT's 89 cap-hit prefixes gets 18 right, Think-SFT itself 18). Observation explained: why neither model rescues Think-SFT's cap-hit prefixes (no graveyard theory explained the language switch).
differs_from: r5-m04 (refuted) and r7-m09 explained Think-SFT's errors by cap hits on long problems or by format; m11 names a language-drift state that makes part of the cap hits unrecoverable. m10 says Think-SFT stays precise at length; m11 says that holds only for traces that stay in English, so at 32k Think-SFT gains less than m10 or m12 predict. m09 is a grading artifact; m11 is a generation state.
holds_against: result-818c20 (cap hits are unfinished reasoning, not loops): drift is not a loop and is consistent with rule A firing on only 6. result-b006f5 (finished answers over 12,000 tokens right 68.2 %): those are the traces that finished, mostly the undrifted ones in m11's reading; it predicts the drifted ones are the ones that do not finish.
first_test: Fetch the four full-text Think-SFT hard328 jobs (iterate-runs abaybektursun-1115-000503-1e5f, -000525-ea4e, -014823-ef56, -014833-1daa). Mark an answer drifted if it holds >= 50 CJK characters (U+4E00-U+9FFF). Statistic 1: v3 accuracy of drifted finished answers over 8,000 tokens minus that of undrifted ones; m11 predicts <= -30 points (refuted if > -15). Statistic 2: share of cap hits that are drifted; m11 predicts >= 0.5. Statistic 3: in the transplant rows (studies/rlneurons/results/transplant/hard328-01) no text is stored, so report instead the cap-hit fall from think to sft1_rl20 on the problems whose Think-SFT sample-0 cap hit is drifted versus undrifted; m11 predicts a larger fall on drifted ones.

mechanism: On long problems the cued base does not stall: it reaches a right answer as a roughly constant-rate event per token generated, set by the problem and the model, so its cap hits at T 1.0 are answers still on the way (not loops, not guesses) and raising the cap to 32,768 tokens converts them at the same rate as the 8,000-16,000 window did, while a forced commit cannot.
starts_from: result-51fd20 (tokens between 8,000 and 16,384 buy 12 problems; forced commits at cap hits right on 0-2), knowledge-787e53 (no rule-A loops at T 1.0), result-5de032 (the base's 77 cap-hit problems are long for RL too: 13,155 tokens mean, 19 right). Observation explained: the base's long answers keep converting to right answers right up to the cap while forcing an answer gains nothing.
differs_from: r6-account-rival says cap hits are the hard end of one difficulty axis and says nothing about what more tokens do; m12 gives a time-to-solution law that sets the 32k score. all-1 / r1-all-1 (refuted) had the base degrade with its own length; m12 predicts a flat hazard. across-2 had a learned budget controller; m12 has no stopping policy at all. m10 is about precision of finished answers by length; m12 about the rate of solving among answers still running.
holds_against: result-51fd20 (forced commit at the cap is right on 0-2 of 77): a commit stops the process before the solve event, which m12 predicts arrives later, not that a partial answer is right. r6-account-rival (cap hits are the hard end of one axis): m12 is compatible with that ordering and adds the rate; it would fail if the solve hazard falls steeply after 8,000 tokens, which its test checks.
first_test: From studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl (attempt 0, all 4 samples) compute, for windows [4k, 8k), [8k, 12k), [12k, 16.4k), the hazard of a right finish = (samples finishing right inside the window) / (token-mass of samples alive in the window, in thousands). m12 predicts the ratio hazard[12k, 16.4k) / hazard[4k, 8k) in [0.6, 1.4] (refuted below 0.4). Repeat on studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl; m12 predicts a ratio in the same range and a level at least 2 times the base's.
